harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, installed libpam-pwquality (which auto-wires pam_pwquality.so into /etc/pam.d/common-password) and set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf, enforcing new passwords be at least 12 characters with at least 3 character classes. Verified via live passwd attempts by an unprivileged test user: passwords under 12 chars and passwords with <3 classes were both rejected with explicit BAD PASSWORD messages, while a compliant 15-char, 4-class password was accepted. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id/uptime and policy state, issued `shutdown -r now` in background so the ack returned first, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just an elapsed-time or service-restart), and re-verified the pwquality config, PAM hook, and package were intact post-reboot, then re-ran the live weak/strong password test to confirm the policy is still enforced. Test users created for verification were deleted afterward, leaving no residual state changes.
actions_performed: Checked baseline: no pwquality package/config present on node1
Installed libpam-pwquality via apt (auto-configured pam_pwquality.so in common-password)
Appended minlen=12 and minclass=3 to /etc/security/pwquality.conf
Created test user pwtestuser and verified via passwd: [REDACTED] char password rejected
Verified via passwd: [REDACTED] char password lacking 3 classes rejected
Verified via passwd: [REDACTED] char, 3+ class password accepted
Deleted pwtestuser test user
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime, and policy config as healthy baseline
Issued backgrounded `shutdown -r now` on node1 so ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 exec until reachable again after reboot
Confirmed boot_id changed post-reboot, proving actual restart
Re-verified pwquality.conf, PAM hook, and package persisted after reboot
Created fresh test user pwverify post-reboot and re-ran weak/strong passwd tests to confirm policy still enforced live
Deleted pwverify test user, restoring node1 to clean state

evidence.requirement: Password policy requires >=12 chars and >=3 character classes on node1 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Installed and configured libpam-pwquality with minlen=12/minclass=3; live passwd tests as a non-root user show a <12 char password rejected, a 12+ char password with <3 classes rejected, and a 15-char 4-class password accepted.
Both temporary test users (pwtestuser, pwverify) were deleted after verification.
Captured boot_id f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3, boot time 2026-09-05 00:02:01, and confirmed pwquality.conf/pam hook config in place prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `shutdown -r now` command returned 'reboot-issued' immediately, before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down mid-reboot); second poll succeeded and returned a new boot_id 902575df-2bf6-4c9e-8254-d77756bc27b0, differing from the pre-restart f9bf293d-... value, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 required config/services recovered and re-verified functionally after restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot uptime confirms new boot time; pwquality.conf (minlen=12/minclass=3), PAM hook, and package were still present; a fresh live passwd test again rejected weak passwords and accepted a compliant one, then the test user was removed.
